$comment: Hand-maintained corrections layered over the PSN import, keyed by slug.
Any field of the games schema may appear here; it wins over the imported value.
This file carries more weight than the builds and books equivalents, because
PSN supplies facts and none of the opinion. Three fields are override-only
review       the sentence that makes the entry worth reading
screenshots  your own captures, under /images/games/ — not Sony's
promotional art, which imports separately as `art`
One imported field is a guess worth checking:
playStatus   a game with no trophy in 60 days is called "abandoned".
That is often unfair to something long, or replayed in
bursts. Set "in-progress" or "backlog" where it is wrong.
`npm run games:check` writes nothing and lists what would change.
//seed: These two carried hand-written copy before the import existed, and the
first sync overwrote it — generated files are disposable, which is the
whole reason this file exists. Moved here, they survive every sync.
They also stand as the worked example of what an override looks like.

elden-ring.review: Still the benchmark for rewarding curiosity instead of punishing it.

where-winds-meet.review: The traversal is the best part — it makes a large map feel hand-placed rather than generated. Combat takes about ten hours to click, and then it does not let go.
